subject: Follow-up: Privacy & network questions for HealthLytics private deployment
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Clara Nguyen <clara.nguyen@healthlytics.com>, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Privacy & network questions for HealthLytics private deployment

Hi Clara / Tom — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and the technical questions I promised to capture so your security and infra teams can triage: 

1) PII scope: you mentioned patient identifiers + limited PHI (diagnostic codes, timestamps). Can you confirm the complete list of fields you consider PII/PHI and whether we should treat embeddings as sensitive for this engagement?

2) Data residency: primary requirement is US-only for the pilot, with a potential requirement for single-state residency later. Confirm if the AWS account/region you want us to deploy into is us-east-1 or another region.

3) Network boundary & egress: you indicated private VPC peering is preferred over internet egress. Can you share whether you prefer VPC peering, PrivateLink, or Transit Gateway? Also confirm whether outbound calls to third-party telemetry (e.g., monitoring agents) are allowed.

4) Retention & logging: what are your retention windows for raw request payloads, generated responses, and audit logs? Any minimums (e.g., 7 years for audit logs) or maximums for deletion?

5) Air-gap/on-prem need: you flagged an air-gapped option for one of your regulated customers — is that an absolute requirement for the pilot or only for a future phase?

I attached the sketched architecture we discussed (healthlytics-proposed-arch.pdf) and a short checklist of the standard items we collect for Private deployments. I asked Rishi and Marissa to weigh in below with initial configuration suggestions based on what you said.

Next steps I propose: 1) Clara/Tom — confirm answers to the five items above by EOD Thursday; 2) we’ll follow up with a tight implementation checklist and a targeted timeline; 3) schedule a 30-min follow-up with your infra/security folks (can do Fri or early next week).

Thanks,
Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: healthlytics-proposed-arch.pdf, redwood-private-deploy-checklist.xlsx
From: Clara Nguyen <clara.nguyen@healthlytics.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@healthlytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 17:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Privacy & network questions for HealthLytics private deployment

Thanks Sergio — great summary. Quick answers below (we'll share a formal matrix later):

1) PII/PHI scope: patient_id, mrn, dob, full_name, email, phone, diagnostic_code, encounter_timestamp. We do NOT consider non-identifying aggregate metrics (e.g., counts) as PII. We want embeddings treated as potentially sensitive for now — please treat embeddings the same way as raw text unless we agree otherwise.

2) Residency: pilot must stay within the US. Preferred region is us-west-2 for latency reasons (our analytics cluster lives there). We can provide an AWS account and a VPC with a private subnet.

3) Network boundary & egress: preferred is VPC peering from our account to Redwood's private endpoints. PrivateLink is acceptable if peering is not workable. No outbound internet egress from the private subnets is allowed except to our logging/monitoring endpoints (we will provide IP ranges). Third-party telemetry outbound is currently blocked.

4) Retention & logging: audit logs — retain 7 years. Raw request/response payloads — retain 90 days by default, with auto-deletion unless specific legal hold flags exist. We expect request/response retention to be configurable per-tenant. All logs must be write-once; no modifications allowed.

5) Air-gap: air-gapped on-prem is NOT required for the pilot; it's a Q3 ask for one regulated customer. For pilot, VPC private deployment is ok.

I'll attach a short spreadsheet with our required IP ranges and a compliance note from procurement.

—Clara
Clara Nguyen
Head of Platform Security, HealthLytics
clara.nguyen@healthlytics.com

Attachments: healthlytics-ipranges.xlsx, healthlytics-compliance-note.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Clara Nguyen <clara.nguyen@healthlytics.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Privacy & network questions for HealthLytics private deployment

Appreciate the quick clarifications, Clara — a few technical notes from our infra team below so you can validate feasibility: 

- Residency & placement: deploying into your us-west-2 account via VPC peering is straightforward. We'll request a peering connection and a dedicated private endpoint subnet (we won't create any routes with internet gateways).

- Network patterns: PrivateLink is an option but requires endpoints in your account. Peering typically gives lower operational overhead for our customers. If you prefer PrivateLink for stronger isolation or to avoid route table changes, we can support it.

- Data handling & KV cache: Redwood does optional prefix/KV caching for repeated prefixes to save cost. For PII-sensitive workloads we can disable cross-tenant caches or run caches in a customer-dedicated mode. We recommend customer-dedicated caches for HealthLytics pilot.

- Retention controls: we support configurable retention for request/response payloads and separate immutable audit logs (WORM-like). Default we can set request/response to 90 days and audit logs to 7 years. Deletion can be automated via lifecycle policies you control.

- Logging: comprehensive audit logs (request metadata, model variant, timestamps) will be written to your S3 bucket with server-side encryption (SSE-KMS). Payload-level logs can be optionally redacted or not stored. Access is controlled via IAM roles we provide for the service account.

- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS) and can integrate with HSM-based key material if required for on-prem future phases.

- Air-gap note: for the Q3 air-gapped ask, we'll need discrete packaging and an offline key exchange process; that's a larger project but feasible.

I'll attach a short SOC2 snapshot and a proposed minimal network ACL template for peering.

Cheers,
Rishi
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-soc2-snapshot.pdf, peering-acl-template.txt

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Privacy & network questions for HealthLytics private deployment

Thanks Clara — perfect, that gives us what we need to move to a scoped PILOT SOW. Action items and timeline proposal: 

1) Clara/Tom: share the AWS account id, VPC id, and the IP ranges sheet by EOD Friday (we have those items on the HubSpot deal).
2) Redwood (Rishi/Marissa): produce a one-page deploy checklist + minimal IAM role spec and an initial peering request template by Monday. Include the retention configuration (90 / 7y) as the default and an option to disable payload logging.
3) I’ll draft a 30-day pilot SOW and pricing (dedicated small pool) and circulate for review by next Wed.

Can we lock a 30-min working session Monday 10am PT to walk through the peering steps with your infra team? If that works, I'll send an invite.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
